svg.aria-label: How to write é è ê: 3 letters, é, è, ê, one after another
svg.title: Writing é è ê
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: é, è, ê (latin). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/LatinPrint-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: é: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class é: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e (commit f6dbd80) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>; è: By analogy with the cited é and ñ, not separately sourced: the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/e/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the grave last, as UJIpenchars2's native Spanish writers draw the marks of é and ñ (UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/e/metadata.json>; ê: By analogy with the cited é and ñ, not separately sourced: the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/e/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the circumflex last, as UJIpenchars2's native Spanish writers draw the marks of é and ñ (UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/e/metadata.json>. Source notes on variation: é: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of é, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are two strokes; the accent is found as a separate mark above the letter in all 120 and drawn last in all 120. Its direction splits: 75 draw it up to the right, 35 down to the left. The e is the Grundschrift-App's e (level kleinbuchstaben/e, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only). The accent is drawn up to the right, as most of these writers draw it; about three in ten draw it down to the left. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the é of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. è: ORDER BY ANALOGY, NOT SEPARATELY SOURCED. No source reachable here records how è is written: the Grundschrift-App has no letter with this mark, and UJIpenchars2 holds Spanish characters only. So its order is drawn by analogy with the cited é and ñ. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) finds the accent of é drawn last, after the e, in all 120 of its traces, and the tilde of ñ last, after the n, in all 108 where it is a separate mark (104 of them from left to right). è is therefore the Grundschrift-App's e (level kleinbuchstaben/e, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the grave after it. No source reachable here records the direction of this mark, so it is drawn left to right and top to bottom, the direction these records give every mark no cited record covers. The grave falls to the right, so it runs down to the right from its upper left end. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are claimed, and only by analogy; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the è of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. ê: ORDER BY ANALOGY, NOT SEPARATELY SOURCED. No source reachable here records how ê is written: the Grundschrift-App has no letter with this mark, and UJIpenchars2 holds Spanish characters only. So its order is drawn by analogy with the cited é and ñ. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) finds the accent of é drawn last, after the e, in all 120 of its traces, and the tilde of ñ last, after the n, in all 108 where it is a separate mark (104 of them from left to right). ê is therefore the Grundschrift-App's e (level kleinbuchstaben/e, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the circumflex after it. No source reachable here records the direction of this mark, so it is drawn left to right and top to bottom, the direction these records give every mark no cited record covers. The circumflex is one stroke, up from its left foot to the peak and down to its right foot. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are claimed, and only by analogy; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the ê of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 2 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 3 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class é: 120 tablet pen traces by
60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e (commit f6dbd80)
Letter 2: stroke order after By analogy with the cited é and ñ, not separately sourced: the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e
(assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/e/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the grave last, as UJIpenchars2's native Spanish writers draw the marks of é and ñ (UCI
Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0)
Letter 3: stroke order after By analogy with the cited é and ñ, not separately sourced: the e after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/e
(assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/e/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only), then the circumflex last, as UJIpenchars2's native Spanish writers draw the marks of é and ñ
(UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
